name: Adjustment-Layer Zoom-Blur Flow
use_when: A short-form edit needs section-level motion polish after the rough cut, captions, and body visuals are working.
A zoom-out reveal or smooth zoom-in can make a hook, filler card, B-roll section, or full-screen animation feel connected.
The same polished motion should be reusable across selected sections.
A CapCut graph zoom needs motion blur after the zoom timing and curve are already locked.
avoid_when: The edit is not yet structurally clear.
The zoom would crop captions, faces, UI, product, or proof.
The adjustment layer would affect the wrong clips or make the edit feel over-presetted.

timeline_pattern.pattern: section_start -> adjustment_layer -> transform_scale_130_to_100 -> gaussian_blur_3_to_0 -> optional_scale_100_to_115 -> duplicate_to_selected_sections -> phone_preview
timeline_pattern.range_rule: Adjustment layers must cover only the intended section.
timeline_pattern.polish_rule: Add these moves after the edit already works without them.
timeline_pattern.reuse_rule: Duplicate the adjustment layer only on moments that need flow or emphasis.

motion.rule: Use an eased zoom-out with blur for a quick reveal, then a controlled zoom-in when a section needs continued motion.

keyframe_values.zoom_out: Start around 130% scale and settle to 100%.
keyframe_values.blur: Start around Gaussian Blur 3 and settle to 0.
keyframe_values.zoom_in: After the settled keyframe, move toward about 115% for a smooth push if crop remains safe.
keyframe_values.easing: Start fast and slow into the settle point; smooth the later push so it does not feel like a jump.
keyframe_values.capcut_motion_blur: For CapCut graph zooms, Blur 10 and Blend 10 can be a starting point after timing lock; lower if readability drops.

sound.rule: A soft whoosh can support the zoom only when it does not compete with dialogue and is not repeated mechanically.

captions.rule: Preview caption-safe crop after every adjustment zoom; text should not drift into platform UI or off-frame.

color.rule: Blur and zoom should not hide proof detail or create unreadable compression artifacts.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use zoompan or crop/scale expressions plus gblur keyframes for previewable approximations; render short section tests.
implementation.remotion: Create an AdjustmentZoom sequence wrapper with scaleFrom, scaleTo, blurFrom, blurTo, pushScale, easing, startFrame, and endFrame.
implementation.blender: Use camera focal length or object/camera scale and compositor blur only for animated scenes that need this polish.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use keyframed scale with graph-shaped easing and blur on an adjustment layer or duplicated clip effect, then copy only to selected sections. For stacked graph zooms, add motion blur after the export/re-import zoom passes are locked.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Place an adjustment layer over the intended range, apply Transform scale keyframes and Gaussian Blur keyframes, ease the curves, then duplicate the adjustment layer to chosen sections.

common_mistakes: Adding zoom polish before the cut, captions, and visual hierarchy work.
Letting an adjustment layer affect unintended clips.
Cropping captions, faces, UI, products, or proof during the push.
Repeating the same zoom on every section until it feels automated.
Using blur so strongly that the viewer cannot inspect the first frame.
Adding motion blur before graph timing, scale, and subject centering are approved.
qc: Adjustment layer range affects only the intended section.
Zoom and blur settle before the viewer needs to read the frame.
Captions, faces, UI, products, and proof remain safe during the move.
The effect is used on selected moments, not every cut.
The section still works when the adjustment zoom is disabled.
If CapCut motion blur is used, are faces, captions, proof, UI, products, and action still readable?
